newsitem.title: USA: Andrew Corp. stock slides after downgrades.
newsitem.headline: Andrew Corp. stock slides after downgrades.

text.p: Shares of Andrew Corp. fell about 20 percent in heavy trading Tuesday after two brokerages cut the telecommunications equipment company's rating.
The stock slid $5.375 to $24 on Nasdaq, where it was among the most active issues in early afternoon trading.

Wessels, Arnold & Henderson Llc, which had previously recommended buying Andrew's stock, downgraded it to hold due to concerns about the company's revenue stream, sources familiar with the report said.
The Minneapolis-based brokerage also cut its revenue estimate for the fiscal year ending in September to $922.2 million from $947.2 million, compared to $793.6 million a year ago, sources said.
Merrill Lynch also downgraded Andrew, which is based in Orland Park, Ill., to near-term neutral from accumulate, but it continued to recommend accumulating the stock for long-term gains.

Andrew's broadcasting business could be weaker than expected in the near term because of the impending switch from traditional to high-definition television, Wessel, Arnold & Henderson said in a research note, according to sources.
